A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, equations, figures and appendices A–H are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original adaptation experiments on GSM8K, FLORES and IFEval, checkpoint comparisons, and additional analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and additionally reports e-SNLI evaluation, script-overhead measurements and weight-compression results.

M1.justification: The data, parametric and inference-control procedures in Section 4, and the combined procedure in Appendix G, are unchanged. Full Model was already described in v1. The newly discussed ZIP compression is explicitly excluded from the main results.

E1.justification: v2 adds natural-language inference using e-SNLI to the checkpoint comparison in Figure 8. The original mathematical reasoning, English–French translation and instruction-following coverage remains.

E2.justification: Figures 3 and 9 now explicitly include Full Model results in the method comparisons, whereas v1 named this baseline in Section 4 but omitted its points from these figures. The other comparators, including the linear-projection baseline, are retained.

E3.justification: The added supplementary checks evaluate script size as a percentage of total program length and ZIP compression through storage reduction and runtime. Existing benchmark metrics, model sizes and stated sweeps remain unchanged. The newly supplied Full Model hyperparameters do not establish a revision to previously used settings.

E4.justification: New Figure 10 examines which methods are sensitive to script overhead, and Appendix B adds a compression-versus-runtime check. Section 7 presents the added e-SNLI evaluation as a check on the post-training data-overlap explanation. The existing combined-method analysis in Appendix G is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new script-overhead distribution summarizes variation across experiments, rather than uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds e-SNLI curves, compression and script-overhead results, and explicit Full Model points. Figures 3 and 9 substantially increase plotted program lengths for translation's parametric methods. Figure 5 changes post-trained Olmo3-7B GSM8K performance from 80.5% to 83.4% and SmolLM3 IFEval from 70.5% to 76.0%, alongside other updates. These revise the reported evidence; their cause is not documented, and Section 7 retains some old values.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds Theorem A.4 and a simulation-based proof of additive-constant invariance under changing the universal machine. It also corrects the conditioning variable in Remark A.2's proof. The central definitions, existing bounds and remaining proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: operationalising superficial alignment through task complexity, unifying three adaptation views, and contrasting pre-training with post-training. The additional evidence does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: The existing post-training overlap caveat gains an explicit rationale for examining FLORES and e-SNLI. Appendix B newly explains that script overhead particularly affects Base Model, ICL and URIAL, and that compression was excluded because of runtime costs. The principal interpretations and limitations otherwise remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents Full Model learning rates of 10^-5 and 10^-6, full-dataset training, 16-bit storage and a 2080-bit script. It also reports compression taking up to two hours. Existing measurement conventions and repository links are retained; task-specific e-SNLI setup details remain sparse.

R1.justification: v2 adds Camburu et al. (2018) for e-SNLI. The remaining cited works and substantive positioning relative to earlier superficial-alignment, compression and probing research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The universal-machine discussion moves from Section 5.1 into an expanded Section 4 explanation. There are localized wording edits, updated publication and acknowledgement text, and changed cross-reference labels. The overall narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the script-overhead Figure 10, expands Figure 8 with an NLI row, and updates method legends and some axes. The previous Figure 10 becomes Figure 11 with its analysis retained. Other changes mainly involve figure placement and text reflow within the existing layout.

improvement.justification: The script-overhead and compression analyses make the central length metric easier to scrutinize, while fuller baseline reporting and the targeted e-SNLI check strengthen the supporting evidence. These gains are limited by sparse e-SNLI documentation and new figure–text inconsistencies: Section 7 still reports 70.5% where Figure 5 now shows 76.0%. Overall, transparency improves modestly without resolving the main methodological limitations.
